title: Private installer: pull Runtime LTS artifacts (pinning + validation) + add rollback guardrails
author: Sahana Iyer
description: This PR teaches the Private installer how to fetch/pin Runtime artifacts from the new LTS channel, verify what it downloaded, and add guardrails around rollbacks so operators don’t accidentally cross incompatible version lines. Motivation: multiple enterprise Private customers asked for a stable runtime line with predictable patching and auditability; the installer needs to be able to (a) select Runtime LTS artifacts, (b) pin exact versions/digests for repeatable deployments, and (c) rollback safely during patch incidents without turning rollbacks into accidental downgrades across release trains. This work is aligned with the runtime LTS branch cut and artifact publishing changes (see redwood PRs for LTS branch tooling and provenance). Changes (installer behavior): Adds a Runtime artifact “channel” selection: `runtime.channel = stable|lts` (default: stable) and supports explicit pinning via `runtime.version` (e.g., `1.20-lts.0`) plus optional digest pinning via `runtime.image_digest` (sha256). When channel=lts, the resolver pulls an LTS manifest from the runtime artifact index, selects the exact image tag, and records the manifest + resolved digest in installer state to make re-runs idempotent and audit-friendly. Adds download/selection validation: verifies image digest matches the manifest digest; verifies the manifest signature when `runtime.verify_signatures=true` using the Redwood public key bundle shipped with the installer (key rotation supported via config override). Introduces rollback guardrails aligned to LTS semantics: by default, rollback is allowed only within the same LTS line (e.g., 1.20-lts.x -> 1.20-lts.y). Rolling back from stable->lts or lts->stable requires an explicit flag (`--allow-cross-channel-rollback`) and prints a warning with a link to the runbook. Downgrading across runtime minor lines (e.g., 1.20-lts.* -> 1.19-lts.*) is blocked unless `--force-downgrade` is set; the CLI prompts for confirmation in interactive mode. Adds a post-upgrade validation step: after deploying runtime, the installer queries the runtime `/health` endpoint to confirm the reported runtime version matches the pinned version (or matches the resolved digest) before marking the install as successful in state. This avoids the common failure mode where a Helm/cluster pull uses a cached tag and operators think they’re on a newer patch. Updates docs + examples: new config keys, supported upgrade/rollback matrix, and a short “How to pin Runtime LTS” section intended for enterprise change windows. Implementation notes: Version parsing is intentionally strict for LTS (`<major>.<minor>-lts.<patch>`). We treat `-lts.<patch>` as required for pinning. (If someone wants “latest patch in line”, that should be a separate follow-up so it’s obvious it’s not fully pinned.) Installer state now stores: selected channel, resolved runtime tag, resolved digest, manifest SHA, and verification outcome. This state is used to implement safe rollback and to emit audit-friendly logs. Testing: Unit tests for version parsing, manifest verification, and rollback matrix. Adds an integration test that runs the resolver against a mocked artifact index and verifies digest mismatch fails closed. Adds an e2e smoke test that simulates upgrade -> rollback within same LTS line and verifies the runtime-reported version. Backwards compatibility: existing configs (stable channel with tag-based selection) continue to work. If `runtime.channel` is unset, behavior is unchanged. Follow-ups (not in this PR): support “latest in LTS line” selection with an explicit opt-in (e.g., `runtime.track=1.20-lts`), and wiring signature verification defaults once artifact signing/provenance is fully GA for Private.

docs: update config reference + upgrade/rollback guide

review_conversation: Connor O'Brien (Release Eng): Can we ensure we’re not accidentally allowing “floating” LTS installs? Enterprise wants predictable installs for change windows. Author (Sahana): Yep—`runtime.version` requires the full `x.y-lts.z` if you’re pinning. I intentionally did not add “latest patch” selection in this PR; follow-up will be explicit opt-in. Vivek Kulkarni (Product - Private): The rollback guardrails are good, but make sure support can override during an incident. We’ve had cases where we need to rollback across channel quickly. Author: Added `--allow-cross-channel-rollback` + `--force-downgrade` for minor-line downgrades; both are logged loudly in stdout and installer state. Miles Thornton (SRE): For post-upgrade validation, the /health endpoint can be briefly unavailable during rollout. Please add retry w/ backoff and a clear timeout. Author: Done—exponential backoff up to 5 minutes, with a final message pointing to the rollback command if validation fails. Marcus Lin (Security): For signature verification, please don’t allow silent success when verification is requested but keys are missing. Also: log the key id / bundle version for audit. Author: Updated behavior to fail closed when `runtime.verify_signatures=true` and key bundle can’t be loaded. Logs now include bundle version + key id used. Naomi Feldman (Compliance): Please ensure we retain the manifest hash/digest in a place operators can export for audit evidence. Author: Stored in installer state and printed at the end of a successful install; also added `rwpi inspect --json` fields (string output) so ops can attach it to tickets/change records. Connor (final): LGTM after the e2e flake rerun is green.
release_notes: Private installer can now install Runtime from the LTS channel with explicit version pinning (`runtime.channel=lts`, `runtime.version=1.20-lts.0`).
Installer validates runtime artifact digest against an LTS manifest; optional manifest signature verification is supported.
Rollbacks are guarded to prevent accidental cross-channel or cross-minor downgrades unless explicitly overridden.
